body.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp array belongs, for every \(n\), to Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class, and its nonzero late rare-arm increments violate their negligible-increment Condition 3(ii). Consequently, if a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that baseline class, then for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\), under each sign of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This transfers only the converse. It transfers neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem.
body.proof_tex:
For every \(n,t\), the two assignment probabilities are
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
They are deterministic functions of every available history, strictly between zero and one, and sum to one. The intensity-properties proposition proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable. These are exactly the relevant binary baseline requirements recorded in the sourced Li--Zhao class lemma. This every-\(n\) baseline inclusion does not use the profile-contract event.

We verify the negligible-increment obstruction directly. Fix a start \(a_\star\) and write
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
Distinct martingale increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. For all sufficiently large \(n\), the cap is inactive at every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\). Therefore the variance \(W_n\) of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error is
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 g(t/n)^2\left\{\frac{t}{q_\star(t/n)}-1\right\}.
\]
Since \(q_\star\ge c/2\) and \(g\) is continuous,
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\int_{a_\star}^1
 \frac{u g(u)^2}{q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), \(g(1)>0\), the regression envelope is zero, and, for large \(n\), the smaller binary assignment probability is \(q_\star(1)/n\). Thus the scalar negligible-maximum ratio in Condition 3(ii) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le n}\frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{g(1)^2 n}{q_\star(1)^2W_n}
 =\frac{g(1)^2}{q_\star(1)^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It is not \(o(1)\), proving failure of the cited Gaussian premise rather than assuming a limit law.

Now suppose the confidence sets are uniformly asymptotically honest over the Li--Zhao baseline class. The every-\(n\) inclusion just proved implies, for the selected two-sign pair,
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
Use directly the finite common-subprobability inequality from the sharp intensity-optimized theorem:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For the start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\), the same theorem gives \(\Delta_n\ge d\) and
\(\eta_n^\star\to\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}\). Event inclusion, continuity of the positive part, and the last bound on \(\gamma_n\) yield the displayed converse. No procedure on the baseline class has been constructed, so neither pairwise attainment nor positive structured-class calibration transfers.
body.justification: The intensity-optimized arrays satisfy Li and Zhao's baseline requirements for every \(n\), so baseline uniform honesty supplies the pair-honesty premise needed by the direct common-void argument.
body.gap: The new family's eventual profile contract is insufficient for this note's all-\(n\) structured-class premise, but irrelevant to its every-\(n\) inclusion in Li and Zhao's broader baseline class.
body.consumer: The proposition transfers only the joint converse; it does not transfer the pairwise attaining allocation or the structured positive calibration algorithm.
